thread:
ashley: quick heads-up — ran a narrow quant sweep on SqueezePlay-7b with our chat canonical slice. early readouts below. leaning to recommend a hybrid route for GTN. want feedback before we put into routing proposal.

kevin: nice. numbers?

ashley: pasted summary: 
```
Model: SqueezePlay-7b
Slice: chat_beam_1k (avg len 120)
Configs:
- fp16 baseline: P95 latency 220ms, cost unit 1.00, quality (f1) 0.92
- int8 (q4_0): P95 175ms, cost 0.78, quality 0.905 (-0.015)
- int4 (int4_dynamic): P95 140ms, cost 0.62, quality 0.89 (-0.03)
Observations:
- int8: small quality drop but < threshold for short prompts; huge tail win.
- int4: quality regressions in multi-turn context, hallucination up on long prompts.
```

maria: do we have slice-level impact? any regressions on user intent classification?

ashley: yes — for intent-class slice (avg len 40):
- int8: f1 0.971 vs 0.975 baseline (ok)
- int4: f1 0.945 (-0.03) — borderline

sam: what's kvcache behaviour? prefix caching might hide real costs.

ashley: good call. measured warm vs cold:
- cold start tokens: int4 speed wins are largest on warm; cold latency penalty similar across q levels due to kvcache deserialization.
- recommend enabling prefix KV caching for GTN and degrade to int8 on cold heavy workloads.

kevin: product ask — recommend single model version for GTN or mixed fleet?

ashley: propose mixed fleet with traffic split:
- 60% int8 SqueezePlay for best balance
- 30% fp16 baseline for high-fidelity paths (longform/generation tasks)
- 10% int4 for cheap low-risk routes (short assistant replies)
Also automatic fallback to fp16 on QA regressions.

maria: rollout plan?

ashley: staged canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% with slice-based monitoring. eval probes:
- latency P95
- avg token cost
- quality delta on prompt set (alerts if >0.02 drop)
Ops: add regression alert to console with prompt-level diffs.

ops-bot: deploy-canary started for SqueezePlay-7b int8 @ canary-1 — logs: `canary-id: sp7b-int8-20260321-01`

sam: any concerns for GTN pricing?

kevin: econ-wise int8 saves ~22% unit cost vs fp16. int4 saves ~38% but quality hit affects retention risk. propose we model user impact before pushing int4 broadly.

maria: sounds good. can you dump the eval set PR and a small pre-req checklist?

ashley: I'll open PR with slice artifacts + evalscript. checklist:
- add prefix KV enabled
- add fallback policy to route to fp16
- add canary monitors (latency/cost/quality)
PR in 30m.

kevin: :thumbsup:
